subject: Human Evolution
title: Could Neanderthals Speak?
description: A short lesson to help you apply Could Neanderthals Speak?.

hook.text: Neanderthals had large brains, the FOXP2 gene, and a human-shaped hyoid. Could they talk?

buildup.text: Their ear bones were tuned to the same frequencies as ours—they could hear speech sounds clearly.

discovery.text: Recent modeling of Neanderthal vocal tracts suggests they could produce most consonants and vowels.

twist.text: Having the hardware doesn't guarantee the software. Complex language needs cultural accumulation too.

climax.text: They likely had some form of speech, but its complexity remains one of paleoanthropology's open questions.

punchline.text: They probably talked. How well, nobody knows.

quiz.question: What evidence suggests Neanderthals could speak?
options: Matching FOXP2 gene, hyoid bone, and ear bone tuning
